title: SEO: Schema.org URL duplication between lib/schema.ts and lib/seo/site.ts
description:
## Problem
lib/schema.ts contains its own URL building functions (buildAbsoluteUrl, buildLocalePath, buildLocaleUrl) that duplicate logic already present in lib/seo/site.ts (buildAbsoluteUrl, buildLocalizedUrl, buildHreflangAlternates).

While schema.ts correctly imports and uses SITE_ORIGIN, it reimplements path normalization and locale URL building instead of reusing the canonical helpers.

## Evidence
- lib/schema.ts lines 31-44: Local URL building functions
- lib/seo/site.ts lines 38-56: Canonical URL building functions
- Both implement similar path normalization logic

## Expected
Refactor lib/schema.ts to import and use buildLocalizedUrl from lib/seo/site.ts instead of maintaining duplicate implementations.

## Impact
- Code duplication increases maintenance burden
- Risk of divergent URL formatting between metadata and schema
- Harder to ensure URL consistency across SEO artifacts

## Related Epic
dekyil-v2-jm3
acceptance_criteria:
- lib/schema.ts removes duplicated locale URL builder logic and reuses helpers from lib/seo/site.ts.
- Schema output URLs remain absolute and locale-correct.
- No schema type regressions are introduced.
- Run npm run build and confirm it succeeds.
notes: Blocked: acceptance_criteria field missing; no test command provided.
close_reason: 4f38a9e Removed duplicate URL building functions (buildAbsoluteUrl, buildLocalePath, buildLocaleUrl) from lib/schema.ts and replaced with canonical helpers (buildAbsoluteUrl, buildLocalizedUrl) from lib/seo/site.ts. Build passes successfully with no schema type regressions.

title: Epic: Apply Vercel React performance best practices
description: Improve Core Web Vitals and runtime efficiency by applying high-impact Vercel React/Next.js rules across the locale app routes and shared components. Success means eliminating avoidable server waterfalls, reducing initial client JS cost for non-critical widgets, and tightening high-frequency client-side render paths without changing UX or i18n behavior.

- Don't change call sites in route files for this task
- Don't introduce cross-request mutable global caches

title: SEO: buildAboutUsSchema has confusing default parameter behavior
description:
## Problem
The buildAboutUsSchema function signature has a problematic default parameter:

```typescript
export function buildAboutUsSchema(
    locale: Locale = "en",
    urlPath: string = buildLocalePath(locale, "/about-us")
): WithContext<LocalBusiness>
```

The urlPath default depends on the locale parameter, but if locale is overridden, the default urlPath still uses the default locale value, not the provided one. This creates a subtle bug where calling buildAboutUsSchema("de") would use German locale but English URL path.

## Evidence
- lib/schema.ts line 140-142
- Current callers always pass explicit urlPath or use the backwards-compatible export, so no active bug
- But the API is confusing and error-prone

## Expected
Either:
1. Remove the urlPath parameter entirely and always derive it from locale, OR
2. Make urlPath required if locale is provided, OR
3. Document the behavior clearly

## Impact
- Confusing API that could lead to bugs
- Inconsistent schema URL generation if misused

## Related Epic
dekyil-v2-jm3
close_reason: cc4a764 fix buildAboutUsSchema url path resolution

title: SEO: Non-locale pages missing hreflang alternate links
description:
## Problem
All non-locale root pages (/, /about-us, /rooms, /contact, /gallery, /conference-hall) have canonical URLs but are missing hreflang alternate language links. This creates SEO ambiguity because search engines cannot discover the locale-specific equivalents.

## Evidence
- app/page.tsx has canonical but no alternates.languages
- app/about-us/page.tsx has canonical but no alternates.languages
- app/rooms/page.tsx has canonical but no alternates.languages
- Same pattern across all non-locale pages

## Expected
Non-locale pages should either:
1. Include hreflang alternates pointing to /en and /de equivalents, OR
2. Be removed entirely if they serve no SEO purpose (since middleware redirects to /en anyway)

## Impact
- Search engines may not associate root pages with locale variants
- Potential duplicate content signals
- Inconsistent hreflang implementation across site

## Related Epic
dekyil-v2-jm3
acceptance_criteria:
- Non-locale public pages include alternates.languages entries for en, de, and x-default, OR those pages are removed with equivalent SEO-safe behavior.
- Canonical tags on affected pages remain correct and consistent with locale URL strategy.
- No route path changes break existing navigation.

title: Investigate: Build trace collection ENOENT error for _not-found page
description:
Review of dekyil-v2-jm3 found a build finalization error during trace collection:

Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/kzoeps/Projects/misc/dekyil-v2/.next/server/app/_not-found/page.js.nft.json'

This occurs after successful page generation (32/32 pages built) but during the 'Collecting build traces' phase. The build completes successfully but this error may indicate:
1. Next.js internal issue with not-found page handling
2. Missing configuration for custom not-found page
3. Trace collection bug in Next.js 15.1.9

Impact: Non-blocking (build succeeds) but may affect deployment or edge runtime optimization.

Investigation steps:
1. Check if custom app/_not-found page exists and is configured correctly
2. Verify Next.js 15.1.9 known issues for trace collection
3. Test if error persists in production deployment
4. Consider upgrading Next.js if this is a known bug

Acceptance criteria:
- Build completes without ENOENT errors
- All trace files generated correctly
- Production deployment unaffected
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause of ENOENT trace error is identified and documented in the issue notes.
- If code/config changes are required, implement them and keep behavior unchanged for public routes.
- Build trace collection no longer emits the ENOENT error for _not-found page.
- Run npm run build and confirm it succeeds.
notes: Root cause: project lacked app/not-found.tsx, so Next 15 emitted the internal _not-found route without a trace file and build trace collection tried to read .next/server/app/_not-found/page.js.nft.json. Fix: add app/not-found.tsx to produce the trace entry; also removed ssr:false from server component dynamic imports and disabled TS incremental to unblock build.

title: SEO: Duplicate sitemap routes causing confusion
description:
## Problem
The site has two sitemap generation routes:
1. /app/sitemap.ts - generates all locale URLs (en + de)
2. /app/[locale]/sitemap.ts - generates locale-specific sitemaps

Both routes output overlapping URL sets, which may confuse search engines about which sitemap is authoritative.

## Evidence
- app/sitemap.ts loops through all locales and generates entries for both en and de
- app/[locale]/sitemap.ts generates locale-specific entries
- robots.ts points to /sitemap.xml (the global one)
- Build output shows both /sitemap.xml and /[locale]/sitemap/[__metadata_id__]

## Expected
Choose one approach:
1. Keep only global /sitemap.xml with all locales, OR
2. Keep locale-specific sitemaps and update robots.txt to reference sitemap index

## Impact
- Potential duplicate URL submissions to search engines
- Unclear sitemap architecture
- Wasted crawl budget

## Related Epic
dekyil-v2-jm3
acceptance_criteria:
- Exactly one authoritative sitemap strategy remains (single global sitemap or explicit sitemap index strategy).
- robots route references the authoritative sitemap location.
- No duplicate overlapping sitemap routes remain active.
- Run npm run build and confirm sitemap routes generate successfully.
notes: Blocked: npm run build fails because next/dynamic uses ssr: false in server components (app/[locale]/conference-hall/page.tsx, app/[locale]/gallery/page.tsx).
close_reason: 17be776 Remove locale sitemap route
